rows.answer:
The punishment for defamation under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860) is simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service [1][7][8].

Conditions and time limits:
- The complaint must be made by some person aggrieved by the offence, except that where such person is a child, of unsound mind, has intellectual disability, is unable to make a complaint due to sickness or infirmity, or is a woman who ought not to be compelled to appear in public according to local customs and manners, another person may make a complaint on their behalf with the leave of the court [5].

rows.answer:
A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail by an officer in charge of a police station or by a Court other than the High Court or Court of Session when arrested or detained without warrant, or when appearing or brought before the Court, except where there appear reasonable grounds for believing they have been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or where the offence is cognizable and they have a previous conviction for an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for seven years or more, or two or more previous convictions for a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for three years or more but less than seven years under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 437 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) [1][4]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- The Court may direct release on bail for a person accused of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment, or with a previous conviction, if such person is a child, a woman, or is sick or infirm under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [1].
